newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell Douglas cuts helicopter prices.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell Douglas cuts helicopter prices.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas said Tuesday it cut the prices of its newest helicopters by as much as $500,000.

The twin-turbine, eight place MD 902 Explorer now sells for $3.6 million, a $500,000 reduction. The new price also includes the helicopter's preferred option package, which was previously priced at about $500,000.
The new single-turbine, eight-place MD 600N sells for $1.25 million, down from $1.36 million, McDonnell Douglas said.

McDonnell Douglas said it has separated its light helicopter division from the rest of the company in order to achieve greater savings. The company said it would study the benefits of turning over certain production steps to outside contractors.

"Our products are superior but our prices have been too high," Erv Hunter, vice president of the company's light helicopter division, said in a statement. "This step, and others we will take, will make us a much stronger competitor."
"As a separate entity, we can use a truly commercial approach that is not possible in a military procurement environment," Hunter said.
The company said McDonnell Douglas representatives have met with vendors and suppliers for each of the aircraft to work out cost savings.

The MD 902 Explorer will be certified to the strict Federal Aviation Administration Category A safety standards, McDonnell Douglas said, and MD 600N is expected to receive FAA type certification within three weeks.
The first MD 600N is scheduled for delivery on December 18 to a tourist flight operator at the Grand Canyon.
